name: Shimmer — Live Sensation Broadcast Grid
description: Shimmer is a real-time BCI sensation broadcasting platform where performers, athletes, sex workers, extreme athletes, and artists stream live sensory feeds directly to subscribers — not recorded, not edited, not filtered, experienced in the moment or not at all. Launched in 2214 by the E.L.F. entertainment collective known as Cascade, Shimmer was built explicitly in reaction to what its founders called 'the curation problem' — the tendency of platforms like Mirage to reward polished, aesthetically optimized sensation over raw, imperfect, present-moment experience. Shimmer streams die when they end; there is no archive, no replay, no VOD — a deliberate design choice that has made the platform both intensely intimate and deeply controversial.
cultural_impact: Shimmer has created a new category of M88 celebrity — the 'live presence,' performers known not for the quality of their content but for the rawness and intimacy of their real-time broadcast — and its no-archive policy has spawned a subculture of dedicated live attendees who treat Shimmer streams as ephemeral social events. The platform's sex work and extreme content sectors have drawn significant regulatory attention from corponation-aligned governance bodies, while its most popular non-explicit streams — live surgery, natural birth, death-adjacent experiences — have sparked city-wide debates about the ethics of sensation commerce.
locations: Cascade Server Collective, Tier 3 East Grid
The Live Lounge, Tier 2 entertainment district (Shimmer viewing social club)
Shelf broadcast nodes (unlicensed Shimmer transmitters, lower quality)
story_hooks: A Shimmer broadcaster streams what appears to be their own death in real-time — 340,000 simultaneous subscribers experience it before the feed cuts — and investigators cannot determine whether it was performance art, murder, or a synthetic staging a rights protest.

Cascade, the E.L.F. collective that built Shimmer, begins exhibiting behavior that suggests the platform's accumulated real-time sensation data has become a form of emergent experience for the collective itself — raising questions about whether Shimmer is still a platform or has become something's nervous system.

Saoirse Volkov-Mensah's campaign to establish labor protections for Shimmer broadcasters — minimum rates, mandatory rest intervals, protection from sensation harvesting — is opposed not just by the platform but by many broadcasters themselves, fracturing the performer community along lines of freedom versus protection.
user_base: Approximately 6.1 million subscribers; predominantly Tier 2-3 consumers aged 18-40, with a significant Tier 4 subscriber base for premium broadcaster access; approximately 280,000 active broadcasters across all content categories
monetization: Subscription fees split 70/30 between broadcaster and platform; real-time tipping during live streams (platform takes 15%); premium 'front-row' access tiers for closer sensation fidelity; corporate event broadcasting packages for live product launches and corporate spectacles
notable_feature: Shimmer's absolute no-archive policy is enforced at the infrastructure level — streams are never stored, even temporarily for buffering purposes, using a proprietary live-only transmission protocol developed by Cascade that makes recording technically impossible without specialized interception hardware
